# Occasion and audience

## What this deck is made for

- Occasion: WHAT IS BEING PRESENTED FOR, SAY A DECISION PAPER OR A TRAINING
- Audience: ONE OF THE FIVE, SO MANAGEMENT, PRACTITIONERS, ENGINEERING,
  ALL-STAFF OR AUDITORS
- Length: MINUTES
- What the listeners already know: THE ASSUMPTION IN ONE SENTENCE

::: {.notes}
This slide is not presented. It stands at the front so that a second presenter
sees in thirty seconds whether the deck fits their appointment.
:::

# What it is about

## The subject in one sentence

THE TOPIC IN ONE SENTENCE, IN OUR OWN WORDS.

## Why it concerns this audience

- WHAT THIS AUDIENCE CANNOT DECIDE OR DO TODAY WITHOUT THE TOPIC
- WHAT GOES WRONG IF NOBODY ATTENDS TO IT

# The content

## HEADING OF THE FIRST CONTENT SLIDE

CONTENT IN OUR OWN WORDS. ONE SLIDE CARRIES ONE THOUGHT.

## HEADING OF THE SECOND CONTENT SLIDE

CONTENT IN OUR OWN WORDS.

# What to do or decide afterwards

## The closing that separates the audiences

- Management: WHICH DECISION IS ASKED FOR, WITH WHICH OPTIONS
- Engineering and practitioners: WHICH ACTION FOLLOWS, BY WHOM, BY WHEN
- All staff: WHICH BEHAVIOUR CHANGES
- Auditors: WHICH EVIDENCE GETS PUT FORWARD

This slide is the reason for the talk. A deck without it is a talk after which
everything stays as it was.

# References

## Standard, clause and edition

- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 6.1.3
- ISO/IEC 27002:2022, 5.15

No text from a standard stands on this slide, neither verbatim nor as a
paraphrase following the structure of the original. A reference is standard,
clause and edition, and anyone who needs the wording looks it up in a licensed
copy. That holds for every slide of this deck and not only for this one.
